definition: Microsoft's former mobile DevOps service: builds, test distribution, CodePush updates, analytics and crash diagnostics. It retired on 31 March 2025, apart from Analytics and Diagnostics, which run until 31 March 2027. Microsoft points builds to Azure Pipelines, distribution to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, and CodePush to a standalone server you host yourself.
example: Northline's builds moved from App Center to GitHub Actions, its crash reports to Sentry, and its CodePush updates to EAS Update.

definition: Signing a binary so stores and devices can verify who built it and that it has not been changed. iOS needs a distribution certificate and a provisioning profile; Android needs an upload key, and with Play App Signing Google holds the app signing key and can reset a lost upload key. Keep the keys in a vault and use them only in CI, never on one person's machine.
example: The shop-mobile workflow fetches the iOS certificate and Android upload keystore from kv-mobile-sign for each build.

definition: Replacing the JavaScript bundle and assets of an installed app without a store release. It cannot change native code, so each update targets a runtime version, the native build it is compatible with. Apple and Google allow it for fixes, but not for new features that skip review.
example: A rounding fix in the basket total goes out with EAS Update to 10% of 3.3 installs, then to everyone.

definition: Expo's hosted services for React Native apps: EAS Build compiles and signs iOS and Android binaries, EAS Submit uploads them to the stores, and EAS Update delivers over-the-air updates. They work with bare React Native projects as well as Expo ones. EAS can hold your signing credentials, which is convenient but means a third party holds your keys.
example: Northline uses EAS Update for JavaScript fixes but builds and signs in its own GitHub Actions workflow.

definition: An open-source tool for automating mobile builds and releases. Lanes script the steps to build, sign, bump build numbers and upload to TestFlight or Google Play, and the match action keeps certificates and provisioning profiles encrypted in private storage the team shares. It runs the same on a laptop or a CI runner.
example: The release lane signs the iOS build, uploads it to TestFlight and sends its dSYMs to Sentry.

definition: Capturing crashes and errors on users' devices, grouping them by cause and counting the users and sessions affected, usually per release. Sentry, Firebase Crashlytics and BugSnag are common for React Native. Application Insights records JavaScript exceptions but does not catch native crashes or group them, so teams often use both.
example: Sentry shows that 3.2's top crash hits 1.8% of Android 12 sessions, and that crash-free sessions fell after the release.

definition: Turning the memory addresses, obfuscated names and bundle offsets in a crash into readable file, function and line. React Native needs iOS dSYM files, the Android R8 mapping file and the Hermes source map, each uploaded for the exact build or over-the-air update it came from.
example: Once the 3.2 source map was uploaded, index.android.bundle:1:482113 became AddressForm.tsx line 88.

definition: A store channel for testing a build before it goes to the public. On iOS it is TestFlight: up to 100 internal testers get builds at once, and up to 10,000 external testers after Beta App Review. On Google Play it is the internal, closed and open testing tracks. It is the first ring of a mobile release.
example: Staff use each build on TestFlight and Play's internal track for three days before 2,000 beta customers get it.
